# Two Changes to Selective Availability

Selective Availability was a feature that deliberately degraded public GPS signals for national security. Its use ended in May 2000, when the US government stopped using it at President Bill Clinton’s direction to make civil and commercial GPS more useful worldwide.

That operational change was distinct from a later procurement announcement. In September 2007, the US government announced that the future GPS III generation would be procured without Selective Availability. The announcement did not switch off the existing feature; it specified its omission from a future generation, making the 2000 policy durable for GPS III.
